title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Evan Liu
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler: improved queueing fairness, added starvation prevention heuristics, refined timeout logic. Expected p99 latency reductions and more stable throughput under mixed workloads.
description: Motivation: the continuous-batcher scheduler was showing unfair queueing in mixed-size request workloads, leading to starvation of low-priority or long-waiting requests and occasional tail latency spikes. This PR reworks the scheduler heuristics to introduce age-based priority boosts, adaptive per-queue timeouts, and queue-length aware weight adjustments. Changes include a compact priority aging mechanism, a new soft-timeout that triggers graceful preemption of long-waiting micro-batches, and a fairness counter that ensures no request group falls below a minimum scheduling share. The implementation is intentionally conservative and gated behind a feature flag (continuous_batcher_v2) so we can roll out gradually. Testing: added unit tests for the aging and timeout paths, integration tests that simulate mixed short/long request distributions, and an e2e perf test against our local perf-canary harness. Observability: added metrics (scheduler_age_seconds, scheduler_starvation_count, scheduler_timeout_events) and traces for decision points. Backwards compatibility: default runtime behavior is unchanged unless the feature flag is enabled. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and performance targets.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial refactor of queue data structures; implement age-based priority boosting; add soft-timeout and preemption logic; tests and metrics. Commits are squashed on merge.
files_changed_summary: Updates to scheduler internals (queue and scheduler modules), added metrics, tests and docs, feature flag gate, and CI job adjustments for perf scenarios.
review_comments: Maya Gupta: Nice incremental design. Can we confirm the amortized cost of the aging step when there are thousands of queues? Suggest using a ring buffer to avoid per-queue scans.
Evan Liu: We moved to coarse-grained ticks and only update the top K queues per tick to bound amortized cost; added microbenchmarks in scheduler.rs to show <1% CPU overhead at 10k queues.

Rafael Torres: The soft-timeout preemption looks good but we need safeguards to avoid preempting already-committed batches. Add a quick state check before preemption. Also please add metrics for preemption rate.
Evan Liu: Added preemption-state guard and scheduler_timeout_events metric. Updated tests to include committed-batch invariants.
Noah Kim: Can we add an integration scenario that mirrors the customer workload that triggered ENG-4218? Would like an explicit regression test for long-tail latency under mixed-size requests.
Evan Liu: Added perf-canary scenario reproducing the original distribution and included the results in the PR description. Also documented rollout steps in the RFC doc.

Rafael Torres: LGTM after the test stabilization and documentation updates.
Noah Kim: Approved. Recommend canary rollout to dedicated pools before enabling on hosted clusters.

perf_results: Local perf-canary mixed workload: p50 ~0ms change, p95 -4%, p99 -7%
Throughput +12% on steady-state batching when feature flag enabled (measured on n1-standard with same GPU fraction config)
CPU overhead of scheduler heuristics <1% at 10k logical queues (microbench)
Starvation count decreased to zero in 30-minute synthetic run that previously showed periodic starvation events
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2026-02-28. Author: Evan Liu. Merge commit message includes RFC link and performance numbers. Feature gated behind continuous_batcher_v2 and rollout plan outlined in docs/rfc/continuous-batcher-fairness.md. Backported to release/2026-02 as a non-breaking opt-in improvement.
notes_for_oncall: If enabled in prod without gradual rollout, watch scheduler_starvation_count and scheduler_timeout_events. Automatic fallback: the scheduler will stop preempting after repeated preemption failures. Rollback: flip continuous_batcher_v2 feature flag to false.
